title: Fleet capacity entropy analysis and restoration plan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: A multi-region capacity shortfall event affected Dedicated customer latency and throughput for ~45 minutes on 2026-03-09. Symptoms: elevated queue length, increased request errors for long-tail jobs, and autoscaler failing to achieve target headroom. Scope: ~12 dedicated pools across two regions, affecting ~8 customers on reserved capacity plans. Goal: restore deterministic headroom, remove modes of regression, and add automated detection to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: Primary cause: a small regression in the autoscaler decision path (metric aggregator window changed from 60s to 600s in an infra PR) introduced excessive smoothing that delayed scale-up decisions under bursty traffic. Secondary contributor: a latent scheduling bug in the fleet controller where node decommissioning retired instances without compensatory pool replacement when concurrent orchestration jobs failed (memory pressure in the orchestration agent). Tertiary: insufficient alerting on per-pool headroom and an absence of an automatic safety-net for headroom below SLO thresholds.
mitigation_taken: Rolled back infra PR that widened aggregator window (emergency revert PR #4512).
Manually bumped reserved instances in impacted pools to restore immediate headroom (+30%).
Activated emergency throttle for best-effort tiers to preserve reserved-throughput SLOs.
Replaced two orchestration agents showing elevated memory with patched instances and forced reallocation.
Opened a fast-path routing rule to route new requests to healthy regions for affected customers.
Notified impacted customers and provided ETA and compensatory credits.
current_actions: Fix: revert-smoke-tests in CI to include metric-aggregation config guard (in review).
Add per-pool headroom metric and alert (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/89).
Instrument autoscaler decision trace logs for replay and offline analysis (work in progress).
Rework orchestration agent memory handling and add canary rollout (scheduled for 2026-03-14).
Blueprint a capacity safety-net that guarantees minimal headroom via emergency burst capacity and throttles low-priority workloads automatically.
postmortem_actions: Implement capacity-entropy detector: anomaly detector that triggers when headroom variance exceeds expected bounds (owner: Rohit, due: 2026-04-02).
Autoscaler config checksum guard: block deploys where production config drift changes smoothing windows without rollout flag (owner: Sienna, due: 2026-03-30).
Sliding-window forecasting: add short-horizon forecasting (5–60s) into autoscaler decision inputs to avoid over-smoothing (owner: ML Infra, due: 2026-04-09).
Per-pool SLA dashboard: surface headroom, queue depth, and time-to-scale with 1s granularity (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-25).
Runbook update: rapid pool reassignment steps, emergency burst commands, and customer communication templates (owner: Oncall, due: 2026-03-18).
E2E test: simulate concurrent node decommission + orchestration retry to validate pool replacement behavior (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-28).
Canary policy: require autoscaler changes to pass a canary where a fraction of pools are exposed to the new behavior before global rollout (owner: Platform, due: 2026-04-05).
Billing/compensation workflow: automate tracking and calculation for impacted customers to streamline credits (owner: Finance Eng, due: 2026-04-01).
Post-deploy KPI sweep: schedule automated guard rails that sample token-level latency and throughput regressions for 24h after scaling-related releases (owner: Release Health, due: 2026-03-27).
